patches.rationale: slugify currently lowercases and strips non-alphanumerics without Unicode normalization, so precomposed accented characters like 'é' are dropped entirely (e.g. 'Café' -> 'caf'). The fix normalizes to NFKD, drops combining marks, then applies the existing ASCII separation and dash-trimming logic unchanged. New regression tests cover the literal example, decomposed/precomposed equivalence, ASCII separation, dash trimming, and ASCII-only output.
contract_tests: tests/test_slugs_regression.py::test_literal_example_cafe_deja_vu asserts slugify('Café déjà vu') == 'cafe-deja-vu' with str input and str output.

tests/test_slugs_regression.py::test_output_is_lowercase_ascii asserts every character of slugify('Café déjà vu') is in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-' and no unicodedata.combining(ch) is nonzero.
